text.tspan: Not started. Bench: the Linux host only, with the vehicle-speed provider, the layer's host processes, the Autoware vehicle velocity converter and an observer independent of the layer.

<'REQ-MW-010'> reqDeliverReferenceVehicleSpeed : FunctionalRequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* The middleware integration layer shall deliver each finite reference vehicle speed sample (VSS Vehicle.Speed, in km/h) from the vehicle-speed provider over Eclipse S-CORE communication to the velocity input of the Autoware vehicle velocity converter, as a longitudinal velocity in m/s equal to the sample divided by 3.6. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-001; scenario SC-MW-001; like for like with AC-MW-010-01 and E-MW-013 of INC-MW-010 (the same signal, conversion and consumer, autoware_vehicle_velocity_converter); owner decision 2026-10-18"; attribute :>> rationale = "The same reference signal, conversion and consumer as in the AAOS SDV realization make the S-CORE realization comparable with it. One deliberate deviation from that wiring: the speed does not travel on /vehicle/status/velocity_status, the velocity input of the AEB node, which by owner decision keeps a source that does not pass through the middleware integration layer, following the safety-path isolation intent of N-MW-004 and REQ-MW-006. The owner of the topic that reaches the converter is proposed in phase 7 (speedTranslationAllocation), and phase 8 chooses the topic names (GAP-MW-033; owner decision of 2026-10-18)."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "test"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when an observer independent of the middleware integration layer sees provider samples of 36 km/h and 72 km/h, carried over Eclipse S-CORE communication, arrive at the velocity input of the Autoware vehicle velocity converter as longitudinal velocities of 10 m/s and 20 m/s."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }
Not started. Bench: the Linux host only, as VC-MW-011, with a provider that can publish non-finite samples.

<'REQ-MW-011'> reqWithholdNonFiniteSpeedSample : FunctionalRequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* If a reference vehicle speed sample is not a finite number, then the middleware integration layer shall withhold it from Autoware. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-001; scenario SC-MW-001; like for like with the non-finite case of AC-MW-010-01 of INC-MW-010"; attribute :>> rationale = "A non-finite value would otherwise reach the velocity consumers of Autoware as if it were a measured speed."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "test"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when NaN, positive-infinity and negative-infinity samples published by the vehicle-speed provider produce no message at the velocity input of the Autoware vehicle velocity converter, while the finite samples published before and after them arrive."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }
Not started. Bench: the Linux host only, as VC-MW-011, with the health proxy node and an observer of its health topic.

<'REQ-MW-012'> reqIndicateStaleReferenceVehicleSpeed : FunctionalRequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* If the last finite reference vehicle speed sample from the vehicle-speed provider is older than 5 s, then the middleware integration layer shall publish a stale indication of the reference vehicle speed on the health topic that accompanies the speed topic of REQ-MW-010 no later than 6 s after that sample, and a restored indication on the same topic no later than 2 s after the next finite sample. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-001; scenario SC-MW-003; like for like with E-MW-014 of INC-MW-010 (health topic /vehicle/status/velocity_status_health, max_age 5 s, a 1 s watchdog period, stale observed 5.8 s after the provider stopped, restored=healthy observed 2 s after the provider restarted)"; attribute :>> rationale = "The Autoware side must be able to tell that the reference vehicle speed is no longer current, and that it is current again. The 5 s bound and the 1 s tolerance are those of the AAOS SDV realization, whose health topic accompanied its speed topic in the same way, so the two realizations compare like for like; the health topic is named with the speed topic (GAP-MW-033). The 2 s restoration bound is the one E-MW-014 observed. That realization only logged its restoration (restored=healthy) and did not publish it on its health topic; here the restoration goes on the health topic, because SC-MW-003 has the disposition restore on the ROS 2 side. The baseline health states (REQ-MW-004) carry the further step to unavailable."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "test"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when, after the vehicle-speed provider stops publishing, a stale indication of the reference vehicle speed appears on the health topic that accompanies the speed topic of REQ-MW-010 no later than 6 s after the last finite sample, and, after the provider resumes publishing, a restored indication appears on the same topic no later than 2 s after the next finite sample."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }
Not started. Bench: the Linux host only, as VC-MW-011, with a way to restart the adapter.

<'REQ-MW-013'> reqDeliverSpeedSampleAtMostOnce : FunctionalRequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* The middleware integration layer shall deliver each reference vehicle speed sample to the velocity input of the Autoware vehicle velocity converter at most once. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-001; scenario SC-MW-003 (a stale, then unavailable, disposition instead of a frozen value)"; attribute :>> rationale = "A last sample repeated after the provider stopped would reach Autoware as a frozen current speed."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "test"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when, after the vehicle-speed provider stops publishing, no further message appears at the velocity input of the Autoware vehicle velocity converter until the provider publishes again, and each delivered message corresponds to one distinct provider sample."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }

Not started. Bench: the Linux host and the AAOS SDV guest under KVM. The host runs the Autoware-based AEBS stack, the frame assembler and the layer's host processes. The guest runs the SOME/IP receiver and the HMI application.

<'REQ-MW-014'> reqDeliverAEBSSignalsInSourceOrder : FunctionalRequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* While the HMI application in the AAOS SDV guest is subscribed, the middleware integration layer shall deliver each AEBS signal frame of the Autoware-based AEBS stack to the HMI application, in the order in which the AEBS stack produced the frames and with inter-arrival gaps below 500 ms. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-002; scope item hmiPathInScope; scenario SC-MW-002; the reused HMI of INC-AEBS-010 shows a stale disposition after a 1 s receipt gap, and its frame source publishes every 100 ms"; attribute :>> rationale = "The HMI can present the AEBS state in source order only if every frame reaches the guest in the order the AEBS stack produced it; gaps below half the 1 s staleness threshold of the HMI keep a running path from showing as stale."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "test"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when, over an AEBS event that runs MONITORING, WARNING, INTERVENTION and RELEASED with the HMI application subscribed, the HMI application receives every frame the AEBS stack produced on the Linux host, in the same order, without a sequence gap, and with inter-arrival gaps below 500 ms."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }
Not started. Bench: the Linux host and the AAOS SDV guest with the HMI application, as VC-MW-015.

<'REQ-MW-015'> reqPreserveAEBSSignalProvenance : FunctionalRequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* The middleware integration layer shall keep each AEBS signal frame delivered to the AAOS SDV guest unchanged, field by field, including the source kind each field carries (native Autoware AEB output, DE4SDV coordinator output or display-derived; hmiPathInScope). */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-002; scope item hmiPathInScope (the per-field provenance INC-AEBS-010 assigns, with three source kinds); scenario SC-MW-002; owner decision 2026-10-18 (the names no System 2 type)"; attribute :>> rationale = "Coordinator output and display-derived values must never reach the HMI relabeled as native Autoware output, and no carried value may change on the way."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "test"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when every frame received in the AAOS SDV guest over an AEBS event equals, field by field and with the source kind each field carries, the frame the AEBS stack produced on the Linux host, so that no field that carries DE4SDV coordinator output or a display-derived value arrives marked as native Autoware AEB output."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }

Not started. Bench: the Linux host with the layer running and each guest domain of the layer up, with a reachability probe in each; someipd serves the guest domain that the HMI path enters. The positive control needs a control socket that the host exposes on INADDR_ANY, or a control window with the isolation off. The case also needs the interface definition of the HMI path: the SOME/IP service definition and the frame contract of INC-AEBS-010. It also needs the layer's mw::com configuration and the gateway configuration of gatewayd and someipd. It needs the vsomeip configuration of someipd and the configuration of the SOME/IP receiver too. For ROS 2 (DDS), it needs the Launch Manager configuration and the launch configuration of the member on the Linux host. It also needs the DDS configuration of the Linux host and the host configuration that makes the DDS ports and port 4721 unreachable from the guest domains (GAP-MW-046). The execution slices author all of them except the frame contract.

<'REQ-MW-016'> reqNoApplicationDataFromHMIGuest : RequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* The middleware integration layer shall carry no application data from the AAOS SDV guest to the Linux host. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-002; scope item hmiPathInScope (the one-way path); scenario SC-MW-004; ASM-MW-031; owner decision 2026-10-28 (the ROS 2 (DDS) criteria)"; attribute :>> rationale = "With no application data flowing back, a running, stalled or failed guest cannot influence the AEBS stack or the middleware on the host; transport control, such as acknowledgements, is not application data. The criteria also cover ROS 2 (DDS) on the Linux host. A host process whose DDS port a guest domain can reach could take data from the guest outside the elements of the layer. So the criteria ask for ports that no guest domain reaches: a property, not a configuration. DDS on the loopback interface alone does not give it. CycloneDDS 0.10.5 binds its receive sockets to INADDR_ANY (ddsi_udp.c:453-456, 479-480), and the guests share the host's untagged network segment. The DDS finding names the elements of the layer. It extends to the other ROS 2 processes on the Linux host only while ASM-MW-031 holds, and the verification checks that assumption on the member."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "inspect"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when two findings hold. A guest domain of the layer is a domain under the hypervisor that the HMI path enters. First, the interface definition of the HMI path and the configuration of each element of the layer declare no endpoint on the Linux host for application data from a guest domain of the layer. Second, no DDS port on the Linux host of an element of the layer, nor, while ASM-MW-031 holds, of any other ROS 2 process on the Linux host, is reachable from any guest domain of the layer. A reachable port of an element of the layer fails the criteria. A verification that finds ASM-MW-031 not holding shows nothing about the other processes, and for them its outcome is inconclusive."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }

Not started. Bench: no run. The case needs the interface definition and the mw::com, gateway, vsomeip and receiver configurations that VC-MW-017 needs, and the wiring of the AEBS stack on the Linux host.

<'REQ-MW-017'> reqNoEmergencyCommandOnMiddleware : RequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* The middleware integration layer shall carry no AEBS emergency intervention command. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-003; ASM-MW-028; refines the direct vehicle-command path option of REQ-MW-006 (reqIsolateSafetyPath) for the S-CORE member"; attribute :>> rationale = "The command keeps its direct path from the AEB node to the vehicle command gate on the Linux host. This does not define the failure-containment criteria of REQ-MW-006, so GAP-MW-029 stays open; REQ-MW-020 keeps the reference vehicle speed carried over S-CORE off the velocity input of the AEB node."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "inspect"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when inspection finds no element that carries the AEBS emergency intervention command. The inspection covers the S-CORE service configuration, the adapter interfaces, gatewayd, someipd, each element of the layer in a guest domain and the interface definition of the HMI path. The path of that command from the AEB node to the vehicle command gate on the Linux host contains no element of the middleware integration layer."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }
Not started. Bench: the Linux host only, with the adapter process in the ROS 2 environment of phase 8 and a way to throw an exception in it.

<'REQ-MW-018'> reqTerminateAdapterOnException : RequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* The middleware integration layer shall abort the adapter process on every exception thrown in the adapter process. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-004; Eclipse S-CORE aou_req__platform__no_exceptions (doc__platform_assumptions, version 1, eclipse-score/score v0.7.2), which applies to every application using the S-CORE SW-platform; ASM-MW-022"; attribute :>> rationale = "S-CORE assumes that the applications using it do not handle exceptions and supports this with an abort on any thrown exception, which acts on the whole process. Within the integration layer the adapter is such an application, the S-CORE services being the platform itself, and the Autoware-based AEBS stack does not use S-CORE directly (ASM-MW-022). The feasibility risk for phase 8 is recorded in GAP-MW-034."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "test"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when an exception thrown in the adapter process, including one thrown inside a library the adapter links, aborts that process."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }
Not started. Bench: the Linux host and the AAOS SDV guest with the HMI application, as VC-MW-015. The bench stops and starts the HMI application and the guest on demand.

<'REQ-MW-019'> reqDiscardFramesWhileHMIUnsubscribed : FunctionalRequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* While the HMI application in the AAOS SDV guest is not subscribed, the middleware integration layer shall discard the AEBS signal frames of the Autoware-based AEBS stack instead of holding them for later delivery. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-002; scenario SC-MW-004 (the guest or the HMI application down); ASM-MW-030; owner decision 2026-10-28 (the margin at the start of a subscription)"; attribute :>> rationale = "A guest that is down or stalled must not make the host hold a growing backlog of frames. Such a backlog could influence the AEBS stack or the middleware on the host. The HMI also must not show old frames as current when it subscribes again. The clock that stamps a frame is not the clock that times the start of the HMI application's subscription. So a discard that compares the two clocks needs a margin before the start of the subscription. Without the margin, the discard could drop a frame produced after that start, which would break REQ-MW-014. GAP-MW-045 records the band that the margin leaves."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "test"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when, while ASM-MW-030 holds, the HMI application receives no frame that the AEBS stack produced more than a margin before the start of its current subscription. The production time comes from the clock of the frame's producer. The start of the subscription comes from the clock that times the start of the HMI application's subscription. The margin is the bound of ASM-MW-030 on the offset between these two clocks. A run in which ASM-MW-030 does not hold does not show the criteria met, and its outcome is inconclusive."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }
Not started. Bench: no run. The case needs the launch configuration of the member on the Linux host, which the execution slices author.

<'REQ-MW-020'> reqNoSpeedSampleToAEBVelocityInput : RequirementCandidate { subject integrationLayer :> DE4SDV_MiddlewareSCOREFraming::scoreMiddlewareIntegrationLayer; statement { language "English" /* The middleware integration layer shall deliver no reference vehicle speed sample to the velocity input of the Autoware AEB node. */ } attribute :>> source = "NEED-MW-003; owner decision 2026-10-18 (the AEB node keeps a speed source that does not pass through the middleware integration layer)"; attribute :>> rationale = "The velocity input of the braking decision stays free of the middleware integration layer, following the safety-path isolation intent of N-MW-004 and REQ-MW-006. Phase 7 proposes that no element of the integration layer publishes that input (speedTopicOwnershipProposal); its publisher in the member product stays open under GAP-MW-033. No freedom-from-interference claim is made."; attribute :>> verificationMethod = "inspect"; attribute :>> successCriteria = "Met when inspection of the topic wiring of the member shows that no publisher of the velocity input of the Autoware AEB node belongs to the middleware integration layer."; attribute :>> verificationStatus = VVStatus::NotStarted; }
The bench of the verification cases of INC-MW-011. System 1 is the
configured product MW-CONFIG-002, which the bench refers to and does
not own. integrationLayer is its middleware integration layer: the
subject that each verified requirement binds. The System 2 test
environment is not part of this definition yet, because it has no
model element (GAP-MW-044). The bench is not a product selection.
The evidence record that each case of this slice collects: the retained
record of INC-MW-010 with the identity of the run added. A record binds
MW-CONFIG-002 as its configurationIdentity. receiptSha256 is the SHA-256
of the receipt that the run ran against, as MW-CONFIG-002 asks of the
evidence that binds it. modelRevision is the Git commit of the DE4SDV
model that the run evaluated. scoreReferenceIntegrationCommit and
that the run built. ASM-MW-021 names the pins of the increment. If
receiptSha256 differs from the receiptSha256 of MW-CONFIG-002, the run
ran against an earlier receipt. In that case, its verdict holds for
MW-CONFIG-002 only if the configuration's own receipt record did not
change. As MW-CONFIG-002 states, the pull request that rebinds
receiptSha256 says whether it changed. A record also binds the
execution environment, the contract, the raw observation artifact and
the observer. A missing or partial record gives inconclusive, never
The System 2 test environment of the phase-10 runs has no model element
yet. By owner decision of 2026-10-28, the System 2 bench is the GCP VM
de4sdv-aaos-build: n2-standard-16 in europe-west4-a, with nested
virtualization, restored from the snapshot de4sdv-aaos-build-20261014.
Two items stay open. The first is the exact System 2 identity as a
model element. The second is the assignment of each case to a bench.
The Linux-side cases can also run on GitHub-hosted runners if the
S-CORE build fits there. The cases that
run need a Linux x86_64 host (ASM-MW-026) with Eclipse S-CORE, the
layer's host processes and the Autoware nodes that each case names.
VC-MW-015, VC-MW-016 and VC-MW-020 also need the AAOS SDV guest with
the HMI application under KVM on that host (ASM-MW-027). The guest
needs the SOME/IP receiver of phase 8 (GAP-MW-038). The inspection
cases VC-MW-018 and VC-MW-021 need no run. They need the
configurations and the wiring that the execution slices author.
VC-MW-017 needs them too, and a run for its reachability probe from
each guest domain of the layer. The next slice adds the System 2 test
environment element and closes this gap.
